learning_objective: 🎯 Get into the field! Master the fundamental skills, rules, court dimensions, and terminologies of major team and individual sports.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every sport has specific measurements. For example, a standard Football field is rectangular (90-120m long), a Basketball court is 28m x 15m, and an Athletics track is typically 400 meters in a closed loop.

These are the basic movements required to play a sport. In Volleyball, it's smashing and setting. In Basketball, it's dribbling, passing, and shooting. In Athletics, it's the start, stride, and finish.
Strategy is the pre-game plan on how to defeat the opponent. Tactics are the in-game decisions made on the spot (like switching from a zone defense to a man-to-man defense in basketball).
A tournament is a series of contests. Common types are Knockout (lose and you're out) and League (everyone plays everyone). A 'Fixture' is the schedule showing who plays whom and when.
Knowing the language of the sport is key. For example, 'Off-side' in football, 'Deuce' in badminton/tennis, 'Free throw' in basketball, and 'Baton' in relay races.

fun_activity.title: 📏 Room Court Measurer
fun_activity.instructions: Use your own feet to measure the length and width of your room. Compare it to a badminton court (13.4m x 6.1m). How many of your rooms would fit inside a single badminton court?

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the exact dimensions of the court/field of at least ONE team game of your choice (very common in practical and theory exams).
📌 Be able to draw a simple Knockout fixture for 8 or 16 teams.
📌 Understand specific terminologies. If asked what 'Libero' means, you should instantly know it's a defensive specialist in Volleyball.
quick_recap: ⭐ Team games require high coordination, communication, and strategy.
⭐ Individual games like Athletics test personal stamina, speed, and technique.
⭐ Rules and measurements ensure safety, fairness, and uniformity in global sports.
